subject: Animation
title: Steven Universe: Representation Matters
description: A quick, practical guide to Steven Universe: Representation Matters.

hook.text: Steven Universe, created by Rebecca Sugar, was the first Cartoon Network show run by a non-binary creator.

buildup.text: The show featured LGBTQ+ relationships, body diversity, and emotional vulnerability as core story elements.

discovery.text: Steven Universe aired a same-sex wedding years before most other children's shows dared to try.

twist.text: Some countries censored or banned episodes containing LGBTQ+ content, sparking international debate.

climax.text: Steven Universe expanded what stories children's animation was allowed to tell about identity and love.

punchline.text: A boy with a gem in his belly changed what cartoons could say.

quiz.question: What made Steven Universe groundbreaking for children's television?
options: It had the highest budget of any Cartoon Network show
It featured LGBTQ+ relationships and diverse representation as core story elements in kids' programming
It was the first animated musical series
